subChunks.title: useReducer — Managing Complex State
subChunks.hookHtml: When state has multiple sub-values that update together, when the next state depends on the previous in complex ways, or when state update logic is getting tangled in handlers, it's time for useReducer. It's not a replacement for useState — it's an upgrade for cases where state management logic has outgrown setter functions.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
The reducer pattern

A reducer is a pure function that takes the current state and an action, and returns the next state:

function reducer(state, action) {
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'INCREMENT':
      return { ...state, count: state.count + 1 };
    case 'DECREMENT':
      return { ...state, count: state.count - 1 };
    case 'RESET':
      return { count: 0 };
    default:
      throw new Error(`Unknown action: ${action.type}`);
  }
}

function Counter() {
  const [state, dispatch] = useReducer(reducer, { count: 0 });

  return (
    <div>
      <p>{state.count}</p>
      <button onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'INCREMENT' })}>+</button>
      <button onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'DECREMENT' })}>-</button>
      <button onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'RESET' })}>Reset</button>
    </div>
  );
}

Actions with payloads

function todoReducer(state, action) {
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'ADD_ITEM':
      return [...state, { id: Date.now(), text: action.text, done: false }];
    case 'TOGGLE_ITEM':
      return state.map(item =>
        item.id === action.id ? { ...item, done: !item.done } : item
      );
    case 'REMOVE_ITEM':
      return state.filter(item => item.id !== action.id);
    default:
      return state;
  }
}

// Dispatch with payload:
dispatch({ type: 'ADD_ITEM', text: 'Learn useReducer' });
dispatch({ type: 'TOGGLE_ITEM', id: 42 });

When useReducer beats useState

Reach for useReducer when:

  • State is an object with multiple related sub-values
  • The next state depends on the previous in complex ways
  • Multiple handlers perform similar state transformations (risk of duplication)
  • You want the update logic in one testable place (the reducer)
  • State changes are complex enough to name with an action type

Stick with useState when:

  • State is a single independent value (boolean, number, string)
  • Updates are simple setters with no complex logic

Vex: "The reducer pattern separates what happened (the action) from what to do about it (the reducer). When you have six different buttons each calling a setter with slightly different logic, you have six places where bugs can live. A reducer puts all that logic in one place."

Initialising with a function (lazy initialisation)

// Expensive initial state — only computed once:
const [state, dispatch] = useReducer(
  reducer,
  null,                          // ignored
  () => ({ items: loadFromStorage(), count: 0 }) // called once on mount
);

storyBeats.text: The workbench has six buttons, each reaching into the same state object through different handlers. Vex circles the handlers with chalk. 'Six places where the same logic lives, slightly differently. Find the bug.'

storyBeats.speaker: Vex the Interface Weaver
storyBeats.text: A reducer is a single, testable function that describes every way your state can change. Instead of calling setState directly from five handlers with slightly different logic, you dispatch a named action. The reducer handles all the cases in one place.

storyBeats.speaker: Todo reducer

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a <TodoApp /> using useReducer:

  • Reducer handles: ADD (add item with text from action), TOGGLE (toggle done by id), REMOVE (remove by id)
  • Render a list of todos, each with a toggle button (data-testid="toggle-{id}") and remove button (data-testid="remove-{id}")
  • An input + Add button (data-testid="add") dispatches ADD
  • Completed items have className="done"
subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a <ShoppingCart /> using useReducer from scratch. State: array of { id, name, price, qty }. Actions: ADD_ITEM (adds new or increments qty), REMOVE_ITEM, INCREMENT_QTY, DECREMENT_QTY (min qty 1), CLEAR. Display total price (derived). No scaffold.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain when to use useReducer instead of useState. Give a concrete example — take a component with 5 event handlers that each call multiple setState calls — and show how converting to useReducer makes the logic clearer and more testable.

questions.prompt: What are the two arguments returned by `useReducer(reducer, initialState)`?
options: The current state and a dispatch function to send actions to the reducer
The current state and a setState function identical to useState's setter
The reducer function and the current state
An action object and a commit function
questions.answer: The current state and a dispatch function to send actions to the reducer
questions.explanation: useReducer returns [state, dispatch]. state is the current state value. dispatch is a function that accepts an action object — calling it schedules a re-render with the state returned by reducer(currentState, action).

questions.prompt: A reducer receives action `{ type: 'ADD_ITEM', text: 'Buy milk' }`. How does the reducer access the text?
options: Via action.text — the action is the second parameter passed to the reducer
Via state.lastAction.text — reducers read the action from state
Via event.data.text — actions arrive as events
questions.answer: Via action.text — the action is the second parameter passed to the reducer
questions.explanation: The reducer signature is reducer(state, action). The action object can have any shape — conventionally it has a type property (string) and optional payload properties. action.text, action.id, action.payload are all valid patterns.

questions.prompt: A form has three independent fields: email, password, and acceptTerms. Should you use useReducer or three separate useStates?
options: Three separate useStates — the fields are independent and each has a simple setter; a reducer adds unnecessary ceremony
useReducer — any multi-field form should use a reducer
useReducer — form state should always be co-located in one place
Neither — use a form library for any multi-field form
questions.answer: Three separate useStates — the fields are independent and each has a simple setter; a reducer adds unnecessary ceremony
questions.explanation: useReducer shines when state sub-values are interdependent or update logic is complex. Three independent form fields with simple value-setting updates don't benefit from a reducer. The useReducer version would be more verbose with no advantage. Use the simplest tool that works.
